anita (AcmeCorp): Hey team, hit a blocker collecting a debug bundle from our Private deployment. Collector uploads keep failing with 403 when posting to the pre-signed S3 URL from the control plane. Request ID from client logs: req=0x7f8a2c.

anita (AcmeCorp): Steps we ran: 1) SSH into private box 2) curl to /api/v1/debug/start -> returns 202 and a presigned_upload_url 3) collector runs and then fails at upload with 403.

anita (AcmeCorp): Attaching snippet from collector.log:```
2026-03-16T18:02:31Z INFO start debug session id=dbg-20260316-01
2026-03-16T18:02:34Z WARN upload attempt=1 status=403 url=https://s3-presign.example.net/.... req=0x7f8a2c
2026-03-16T18:02:34Z DEBUG http.response.headers: {"x-amz-request-id":"ABC123","x-amz-id-2":"/..."}
```

anita (AcmeCorp): We tried a manual curl PUT to the presigned url and got 403 too. curl output:```
curl -v -T debug.tar.gz "<presigned_url>"
> PUT /... HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
```

sara (Support): Thanks @anita — sorry you're blocked. Can you paste the exact presigned URL (obscure the bucket/key if needed) and the control-plane request_id? Also which collector version?

anita (AcmeCorp): Presigned URL (redacted): https://s3-presign.example.net/abc?X-Amz-Algorithm=...&X-Amz-Signature=REDACTED
Control-plane request_id: cp-req-20260316-99
Collector version: 1.8.2-private (sha: 9a3f7d)

sara (Support): OK. @mike can you take the lead? sounds like presign mismatch or IP restriction on the Private control plane.

mike (eng-collector): On it. Two quick checks: 1) does your private network have an egress proxy that might rewrite auth headers? 2) can you run the curl with --trace-ascii to get full TLS/headers?

anita (AcmeCorp): We do have a transparent outbound proxy for egress. I can run the trace now, will share.

collector-bot: debug-bundle dbg-20260316-01 created, id=f7b2ea, size_estimate=42MB

anita (AcmeCorp): Trace output (sensitive bits redacted):```
== Info:   Trying 10.0.0.12:443...
> PUT /abc HTTP/1.1
> Host: s3-presign.example.net
> User-Agent: curl/7.79.1
> Accept: */*\r
> Content-Length: 430234\r
> Expect: 100-continue\r
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< x-amz-request-id: ABC123\r
< x-amz-id-2: /...\r
```

anita (AcmeCorp): Proxy does not seem to modify headers. It does terminate TLS for inspection though. Could that break the signature?

mike (eng-collector): If the proxy re-signs or re-encrypts traffic, it shouldn't change the presigned URL itself, but if the proxy alters request body (chunking/length) or strips one of the X-Amz headers, S3 will reject. Also check clock drift on the host (presigned URLs are time-limited).

eli (eng-ml): Adding: the collector uploads include a Content-MD5 header by default in 1.8.x. If the proxy recomputes body or alters chunking, MD5 won't match -> 403. Can you check collector.log for content-md5 computed?

anita (AcmeCorp): collector.log shows: content_md5=Q2hlY2s= (placeholder) and local clock is NTP-synced.

mike (eng-collector): Next repro step: run the collector with increased uploader verbosity and --no-md5 to test. Command:```
./collector --collect debug --upload-verbosity=debug --uploader-opts "no_md5=true" --id f7b2ea
```

anita (AcmeCorp): Running now. If that works we can narrow it down. Also can you generate a new presigned url with a longer ttl so we can test without racing?

sara (Support): We can generate a longer-ttl presigned URL for this run. @mike do you need the original cp-req id to check server logs?

mike (eng-collector): Yes please. Also include the full /api/v1/debug/start payload (headers + body) so I can correlate.

anita (AcmeCorp): Pasted start payload (sensitive fields removed):```
POST /api/v1/debug/start HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
{"target":"collector","level":"debug","redaction":"default"}
```

anita (AcmeCorp): OK retried collector with no_md5 and verbose uploader -> upload succeeded! collector.log now shows status=200 and upload complete.

anita (AcmeCorp): So MD5 appears to be the culprit. Any idea why proxy would break MD5? It does TLS termination + re-encryption and also does some content scanning that may chunk requests.

mike (eng-collector): That fits. The hashing is over the body bytes as seen by the collector before proxy. If proxy re-chunks or injects/strips bytes (e.g., newline adjustments) MD5 won't match. Two options: 1) We change collector to not send Content-MD5 on presigned PUTs for Private deployments behind proxies (safer), 2) update control plane presigning to include fields that accommodate proxies. Short-term: we'll accept bundles uploaded with no_md5.

eli (eng-ml): From a security standpoint, we should avoid disabling MD5 globally. For Private we can detect proxy env and disable only for that route. But need a code/ops ticket.

sara (Support): For now I've asked our control plane to issue a new presign with ttl=10m and accepted_upload_md5=false flag for this run (internal control plane API). That should let you upload normally.

anita (AcmeCorp): Confirmed new presign works with default collector settings. Upload completed, bundle id=f7b2ea, size=47MB.

collector-bot: bundle-uploaded id=f7b2ea status=available location=private-acme/20260316/f7b2ea.tar.gz

oncall-bot: Creating secure transfer ticket to fetch bundle from private storage; ticket ID=ST-20260316-77. Only Support+Eng have access.

mike (eng-collector): I'll open a follow-up issue to detect transparent TLS proxies by checking if Content-MD5 is honored. Proposal: collector auto-detects 403 after presign and retries with no-md5 once, logging diagnosis metadata.

anita (AcmeCorp): That would be very helpful. Thanks everyone for quick turnaround.

sara (Support): Marking resolved for this thread; follow-up issue created: RFC-collector-proxy-md5. We'll keep you posted on timeline. :thumbsup:

anita (AcmeCorp): Thanks! Closing on our side too.
